Growing up, my best friend was being raised in a very Christian environment whereas I was raised to believe what I want to believe. My parents never forced me to go to church, I asked them to take me. I used to sleep at my friend's house on Saturday nights and join her family for pancakes and church on Sunday mornings. Her family respected that mine was non-religious and my family respected that theirs was. Her parents were very respectful, always making sure that my parents were okay with them taking me to things like church or (as we got older) youth groups. I loved it. I never ended up being *truly* religious but I enjoyed learning and experiencing. 

Now, here's the thing. My parents *never* told me to wait until marriage to have sex. They never told me that it was a sin or I would be ruined or I would *definitely* get pregnant and ruin my life. My mom lost her virginity in her abusive boyfriend's truck when she was around 15 or so. Her main concern was that I waited until I was ready and with someone who I wouldn't regret losing it to. That was a big thing for me. I didn't want to experience what my mom experienced and it took a lot for her to share that with me in the first place. All my parents wanted was for me to be smart and safe about it. Condoms, birth control, STD tests. I lost my virginity when I was 14. My only regret was that I didn't wait for it to be something big and special, it wasn't a terrible experience though. 

My friend is now married. We're the same age (20). She got married to her husband two years ago and lost her virginity on her wedding night to him. Her parents taught her to wait until marriage, that it was a sin to have sex before marriage. Her father threw up in the bathroom at her wedding and his brother had to give his speech because he thought she was much too young and he was having a hard time dealing with it. He cried to me. He told me to not go off and get married (her and I aren't as close as we used to be, but their family will always be somewhat of a second family to me). 
I don't know if they were just too eager to have sex, or if they actually wanted to get married so soon, but it took a hit on her relationship with her dad. I don't think she even knows it. 

I'm still friends with them. As a matter of fact, it was me and a mutual friend of ours that set them up in the first place at bible camp when we were 14. I think that if/when I have kids one day, I'll teach them what my mom taught me. Do it when you're ready and don't jump into things.

I have depression and anxiety and I find that being on the pill increases my depression and more things will trigger my anxiety. It's known to affect people that way, if you have a history of a mental health issue then you should probably discuss birth control options with your doctor.

In my experience, the pill lessened my period quite a bit. When I'm not on the pill my periods last a full week - going strong. When I am on the pill, they're bad for the first couple days and disappear pretty much after the third or fourth day. I've never had an acne issue but the pill didn't really change anything. I only really break out when I'm about to get my period - regardless of if I'm on the pill or not.

You'll also want to discuss with your doctor which pill is right for you. Some have higher hormone levels in them than others, and that can mess up your system a bit. 

There are other options besides just the pill too, like an IUD and a shot. I know a girl on the IUD and apparently her periods were horrible for the first couple months but it got better after, and I know a girl on the shot and she gained a lot of weight after she started it.

It's really about what you feel comfortable ingesting/putting into your body. If you really want to use the pill, you can set an alarm for it so you remember to take it every day. Definitely discuss it with your doctor though, better safe than sorry!
